NEPA Clean Energy Analysis: Deliverable 4

Multi-State and Multi-Department Projects

Published

February 23, 2026

Key Decisions
  • What do we think about the “Interstate Connections Map”?
  • Do the top multi-state and multi-department connections make sense?
  • Do we want to explore a sub-agency classifications analysis?
  • Are there any further analyses?

Executive Summary

Key Findings
  • Multi-state projects represent a subset of clean energy projects that span state boundaries, often involving transmission lines or large-scale renewable energy connections
  • Multi-department projects are relatively rare but involve coordination between multiple federal departments
  • Multi-department projects are only Categorical Exclusions (CE): Among clean energy projects, all 21 multi-department projects are CEs; no EA or EIS projects have multiple lead agencies
  • Geographic patterns reveal regional clusters of interstate cooperation

This report aims to create the following set of deliverables:

Data on geography/project location; whether projects are multi-state or multi-agency

It analyzes clean energy projects that cross administrative boundaries—either spanning multiple states or involving multiple federal agencies. These projects often represent larger, more complex undertakings that require coordination across jurisdictions. Table 1 summarizes the number of multi-state and multi-department projects found among our clean energy sample.

Table 1: Summary of cross-boundary projects
Category Count
Multi-state projects 857
Multi-department projects 21
Note that some tables and figures below are filtered for clarity: the state connections table shows only state pairs with 5+ shared projects, the interstate map shows only state pairs with 10+ shared projects, and the top connections table shows the 10 highest-volume corridors.

Multi-state projects are far more common than multi-department projects, likely reflecting the geographic nature of energy infrastructure (transmission lines, pipelines) versus the rarity of projects requiring formal coordination between federal departments.

Multi-State Projects

Multi-state projects are those where the project footprint extends across state boundaries. These typically include:

  • Interstate transmission lines
  • Pipeline connections
  • Large renewable energy projects near state borders

Multi-Department Projects

Multi-department projects involve coordination between multiple federal departments (e.g., DOE and DOI, or BLM and Forest Service). These are relatively rare but often represent significant undertakings.

Notably, all 21 multi-department clean energy projects are Categorical Exclusions (CE); no Environmental Assessments (EA) or Environmental Impact Statements (EIS) have multiple lead agencies in the dataset. We also checked for potential multi-agency involvement by examining whether any agency name appearing in the lead_agency field also appears in the project_sponsor field, which could indicate coordination not fully captured in the lead agency metadata. This analysis did not reveal significant additional multi-agency patterns beyond what is already captured.
